questions.question_text:
One earthquake has a ground amplitude $1000$ times that of another.
Richter magnitude is given by $M=\log_{10}A$.
What is the difference between the two magnitudes?

options.why: Treated the scale as linear, reading the amplitude ratio straight off as the difference in magnitude.
Gave the base of the scale rather than the index that produces the ratio.
Divided the ratio by the base once instead of taking its logarithm.

questions.question_text:
Sound level is given by $S=10\log_{10}\dfrac{I}{I_{0}}$.
A machine's sound intensity is multiplied by $1000$.
By how many decibels does its level rise?

options.why: Took $\log_{10}1000=3$ but left out the factor of $10$ in the decibel formula.
Treated the scale as linear, adding the intensity ratio straight to the level.
Multiplied the intensity ratio by $10$ instead of taking its logarithm first.

questions.question_text:
The hydrogen-ion concentration of a solution is multiplied by $100\,000$.
Using $pH=-\log_{10}M$, how does the pH change?

options.why: Missed the minus sign in $pH=-\log_{10}M$, so the direction of the change is reversed.
Treated the scale as linear, subtracting the concentration ratio from the pH.
Treated the scale as linear and also missed the minus sign in the formula.

questions.question_text:
Star magnitudes satisfy $m_{1}-m_{2}=-2.5\log_{10}\dfrac{b_{1}}{b_{2}}$, where $b$ is brightness.
Star X has magnitude $3.5$ and star Y has magnitude $6.0$.
How many times brighter is star X than star Y?

options.why: Treated the scale as linear, reading the difference in magnitude as the brightness ratio.
Raised $10$ to the magnitude difference of $2.5$ without dividing by the factor $2.5$.
Multiplied the magnitude difference by $2.5$ instead of dividing by it.

questions.question_text:
One air-conditioning unit measures $54$ dB.
Four identical units run together, giving four times the sound intensity.
Using $S=10\log_{10}\dfrac{I}{I_{0}}$, what is the sound level of the four units, correct to one decimal place?

options.why: Multiplied the decibel reading by $4$, treating the scale as linear.
Added $4$ decibels because there are four units, instead of adding $10\log_{10}4$.
Added $10$ dB for each of the three extra units rather than $10\log_{10}4$ in total.
Read the rise of $2$ on the logarithmic axis as the growth factor itself.
Divided the final reading $5$ by the starting reading $3$ instead of subtracting them.
Multiplied the rise of $2$ by $10$ rather than raising $10$ to that power.

questions.solution_text:
At $t=0$ the graph reads $3$ and at $t=40$ it reads $5$.
$5-3=2$
$\dfrac{V_{40}}{V_{0}}=10^{2}$
$=100$
The investment grew to $100$ times its starting value.

questions.question_text:
Richter magnitude is given by $M=\log_{10}A$, where $A$ is the ground amplitude.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: A magnitude-$7$ earthquake has $100$ times the ground amplitude of a magnitude-$5$ earthquake.
A magnitude-$7$ earthquake has twice the ground amplitude of a magnitude-$5$ earthquake.
options.why: Divided the magnitudes, treating the scale as linear when it records indices.

options.text: A magnitude-$7$ earthquake has $10$ times the ground amplitude of a magnitude-$5$ earthquake.
options.why: Used a magnitude difference of $1$ rather than the actual difference of $2$.

options.text: A magnitude-$7$ earthquake has $2$ more units of ground amplitude than a magnitude-$5$ earthquake.
options.why: Read the difference in magnitude as a difference in amplitude rather than as an index.

questions.solution_text:
$7-5=2$
$\dfrac{A_{1}}{A_{2}}=10^{2}$
$=100$
The magnitude-$7$ earthquake has $100$ times the ground amplitude.

questions.question_text:
A workshop tool's sound intensity is reduced to one quarter of its original value.
Using $S=10\log_{10}\dfrac{I}{I_{0}}$, by how many decibels does its level fall, correct to one decimal place?

options.why: Found $\log_{10}4=0.602$ but left out the factor of $10$ in the decibel formula.
Treated the scale as linear, subtracting the intensity ratio of $4$ from the level.
Costed each halving at $6$ dB instead of $3$ dB, so doubled the true drop.
